messages:
elaine: heads up — Acct `acme-inc` reported ~15k credits missing overnight. They run a nightly ingest->embed pipeline. Noticed spike between 03:00-04:00 UTC. Any quick hypotheses? :thinking:
support-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4021 — sudden credit consumption detected for account acme-inc. Automated billing alert triggered.
ryan: do we have request_ids or example payloads from customer? embeddings vs rerank?
elaine: customer says embeddings only. pasted their minimal request from support convo:
```bash
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXXX
{
  "model": "embed-lite-2",
  "input": "...batch of 10k small docs...",
  "idempotency_key": null
}
```
elaine: their worker retries on 5xx and the job scheduler re-enqueues on failure; looks like we got ~12 replays for a subset of batches.
marta: could be duplicate worker runs + no idempotency header. We recently merged the change that removed automatic dedupe on the queue for fast retry mode (PR #1249). That would allow multi-run fanout if the callback was slow.
oncall-aaron: attaching runtime traces from our side for that customer window: request_rate for embeddings endpoint jumped x4 at 03:12, latency spiked, then a cascade of retries from the job service with same payload hash. snippet:
```
[03:11:58] job-scheduler enqueue job_id=jq-893
[03:12:01] worker-1 start job jq-893 payload_hash=0x7c2
[03:12:04] worker-1 -> embeddings req id=req-7c2 status=500
[03:12:05] job-scheduler reenqueue job jq-893-retry payload_hash=0x7c2
[03:12:05] worker-2 start job jq-893-retry payload_hash=0x7c2
[03:12:07] worker-2 -> embeddings req id=req-8f5 status=500
[03:12:08] job-scheduler reenqueue job jq-893-retry2 ...
```
noncall-aaron: you can see there was no dedupe lock — multiple workers executed identical batches within seconds.
ryan: that matches support logs where they saw the 15k credit drop concentrated around that time. How many tokens/embeds per batch?
elaine: ~12,000 small text chunks across ~60 batches, each batch ~200 embeddings. Each failed attempt still consumed tokens because the embeddings service error occured after tokenization/consumption stage.
marta: actionable items: 1) disable fast-requeue in job-scheduler for that customer (stop immediate reenqueue), 2) patch scheduler to include run_id-based dedupe lock OR require idempotency_key header in ingest client, 3) issue credits refund to acme-inc for duplicate attempts.
ryan: I can take the refund flow. Suggest compute exact burn: look at request ids and aggregate successful+failed calls for that account between 03:00-04:00. I'll open billing adj and propose refund amount.
elaine: steps to reproduce (dev): run local job-scheduler with fast-requeue enabled, mock embeddings to return 500 for first two attempts and slow callback. You should see 3+ workers pick same payload. Repro script attached to thread (dev run shown inline):
```
# repro.sh (pseudo)
start_scheduler --fast-requeue &
start_worker --concurrency 2 &
# send 1 batch with no idempotency_key
curl -X POST http://scheduler.local/enqueue -d '{"payload": "batch-A", "account": "acme-inc"}'
# stub embeddings to return 500 for 5s
```
marta: I'll prepare a small patch to reintroduce a short-lived dedupe lock (30s) keyed on payload_hash+account and add metrics for duplicate_runs. Will target a hotfix branch.
oncall-aaron: after hotfix, we should run a scan for other customers with >2 duplicate runs in same minute window and proactively offer refunds. I can add a quick query.
ryan: billing adj created: BA-5621, provisional refund calc in comments. I'll coordinate with finance to expedite.
elaine: customer contacted; we've paused their scheduled ingest for now and offered temporary promo credits while we investigate. They asked for ETA.
marta: ETA for hotfix: ~3h (hotfix branch + smoke + deploy to prod). Will update.
elaine: thanks — please post the PR and I'll mark customer update. :thumbsup:
ryan: once refund done I'll post amount in this thread.
support-bot: Incident INC-2026-4021 status updated: investigating -> mitigation in progress.
